key_insight: AIPatient Arena shows that medical LLMs can sound strong in interviews and explanations, but still struggle with ambiguity, coverage, and diagnostic reasoning in realistic multi-turn consultations.
clinical_relevance: For clinical AI assessment, workflow-oriented and EHR-grounded evaluation is more informative than checking only final-answer accuracy.
method: Built an EHR-grounded patient-specific knowledge graph for multi-turn physician-patient interactions
Evaluated LLMs across 8 competency dimensions in consultation workflows
Tested on 437 primary patients plus 119 and 67 out-of-distribution validation patients
evidence_signal: Across the abstract’s evaluations, LLMs scored highest on questioning, professionalism, and explanation clarity, but notably lower on ambiguity handling, information coverage, and diagnostic accuracy.
watch_item: Better conversation context improved diagnosis somewhat, but gains in treatment planning were limited, so deployment should not rely on static benchmark performance alone.
paper_title: AIPatient Arena: EHR-grounded evaluation of large language models in end-to-end clinical consultation workflows
